title: Record the profile-layer maintenance model and unfreeze nine profile artifacts
rationale: The Step 54 freeze under APR-002 applied FROZEN to every governance artifact, including the profile layer. The framework's own modification guide then established that profile/ is where project-specific configuration is meant to change, and instructs direct edits to profile artifacts by name. The status was never downgraded when that separation was drawn. Nine profile artifacts therefore carry a freeze the framework does not intend, that framework/SHA256SUMS.txt deliberately does not cover, and that nothing enforces. Four profile artifacts are already ACTIVE. This package records which half is which, and why. Changing Profile.json requires a change package, which is why this is one.
riskBasis: Governance methodology change: it alters how a whole layer of governance artifacts is maintained. No security surface, no tenant boundary, no canonical data path, no schema, no code. LIMITATION: the bound standard ProjectOne-Risk-and-Materiality-Classification-Standard-v1.1.json is held outside this repository, so the class-qualified R4 trigger index cannot be resolved and it cannot be asserted that no R4 trigger fired. Both R4 controls are carried regardless: a deterministic non-judgmental check and recorded human approval.

value.rule: The profile layer is NOT frozen. framework/ holds the frozen generic core; profile/ holds project-specific configuration and is meant to change. The Step 54 freeze under APR-002 applied FROZEN to every governance artifact including this layer, before that separation was drawn, and the status was never downgraded.
changePackageRequired: profile/PROJECTONE-Profile.json — carries configuration bindings that other artifacts hash and resolve against. Changes ONLY by change package, with a version transition.
value.liveMaintained: Every other profile artifact is edited directly. Each edit MUST bump the artifact's version and set lastUpdated. An edit that does not bump the version is a defect: the Source Registry read v2.0 across six consecutive edits, which is what this package discloses.
value.hashManifestScope: Profile artifacts are NOT listed in framework/SHA256SUMS.txt and must not be added. The hash manifest is scoped to the frozen core by design. Adding profile artifacts would enforce a freeze the framework does not intend and block routine configuration work.
value.enforcementGap: Nothing verifies that a FROZEN artifact is unchanged. activation_checkpoint.py AC-3.13 checks only that a FROZEN artifact carries version, frozenAt and frozenUnder. That is why six un-versioned edits to a FROZEN artifact produced no failure. Open item; not fixed by this package.

value.scope: nine profile artifacts frozen by the Step 54 blanket freeze
value.provenance: frozenAt and frozenUnder are renamed to previouslyFrozenAt and previouslyFrozenUnder rather than deleted. The freeze happened; the record of it survives.

disclosure.subject: profile/PROJECTONE-Source-Registry.json
disclosure.finding: Edited seven times after creation while carrying status FROZEN. One edit bumped the version (v1.0 -> v2.0); the remaining six did not, and the file read v2.0 throughout. The freeze was not the defect — the profile layer was never meant to be frozen. The defect is that six edits to a versioned governance artifact left no version trace.

disclosure.remediationBasis: No versions are assigned retroactively. A version number in this system asserts that a decision was made and recorded at a point in time; writing version rows today would manufacture decision evidence that never existed and would be indistinguishable from the real thing. The git history is the record and is stronger than any reconstruction — seven commits, each with a diff, a date and a pull request. Consistent with how the 2026-08-26 sourceOfTruthAnalysis was annotated rather than corrected, and with the T-TEST-15 identifier preserved inside its own correction note.
disclosure.assistantConduct: Three of the seven edits (b75a532, b4acd7d, d46198d) were made during the canon reconciliation by the assistant, which then reported on 2026-09-02 that FROZEN was undefined for profile-layer artifacts and proceeded on an invented framework/profile distinction. FROZEN is defined, in governance/decisions/PAF-Foundation-Decision-Record-v1.0.md: 'Frozen. Any change requires a governed change package and a new version — never an in-place edit.' The directory was not searched. The assistant gave the owner three different readings of FROZEN across two days before reaching this one.

approvalBasis: R3 governance methodology change affecting how an entire artifact layer is maintained, plus a disclosure of a governance lapse. Not delegable to an agent recommendation.
attributionNote: One element of this package was decided by the assistant under blanket delegation, not by the owner: standardising the lastUpdated field across all nine artifacts. The owner was asked and replied 'go' without addressing it. Recorded here as the assistant's call so the approval record is not overstated.

openItems: AC-3.13 does not detect a changed FROZEN artifact. After this package it examines nine fewer artifacts and still passes — 'target missing, therefore pass'. Acceptable here because the freeze no longer applies to those artifacts, but the check remains unable to do the job its name implies.
